texts.preamble: Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Author: Madhav J. Jamdar Bench: Madhav J. Jamdar 2025:Bhc-As:51046 603-Aba-2492-202 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Anticipatory Bail Application No. 2492 Of 2023 Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate ...Applican Versus The State of Maharashtra ...Responde Mr. Tushar Sonawane, for the Applicant. Ms. R.V. Newton, App, for the Respondent-State. Coram: Madhav J. Jamdar, J.
texts.facts: By present Application, the Applicant is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with C.R. No. 112 of 2023 registered on 26 th May 2023 under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328, 420, 465, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and for the offence punishable under Sections 26(2)(i), 26(2)(ii), 26(2)(iv) 27(3)(e), 30(2)(a) and under Section 59 of the Food Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147231088/ 1 Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSSA") with Igatpuri Police Station, District Nashik (Rural). Page 1 ::: Uploaded on - 25/11/2025 ::: Downloaded on - 2 603-ABA-2492-2023.ODT Akash Tayde 3. As per the prosecution case the Applicant was dealing with contraband material which is unsafe and dangerous for the health of people. except the offence under Section 328 of IPC, all other offences are bailable offences.
texts.arguments: He submits that as far as Section 328 of IPC is concerned, the Supreme Court is considering the applicability of Section 328 of IPC to the similar cases. He therefore, states that the Anticipatory Bail be granted. 5. On the other hand, Ms. Newton, learned APP strongly opposes the Anticipatory Bail Application. She submits that the offence is very serious and therefore, the Anticipatory Bail Application be rejected. Learned APP submits that there is one antecedent being C.R. No.246 of 2020 registered on 03 rd October 2023 with Kasarvadawali Police Station, Thane for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 269, 272, 273, 328 read with 34 of Rajkumar Balasaheb Sapate vs The State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147231088/ 2 IPC, Section 51(b) of Disaster Management Act, 2005 and under Section 26(2)(i), 27(2)(e), 26(2)(iv), 30(2)(a) and 59 of the FSSA. Page 2 ::: Uploaded on - 25/11/2025 ::: Downloaded on - 26/11/2025 20:38:17 ::: 603-ABA-2492-2023.ODT Akash Tayde 6. Learned APP submits that if this Court is inclined to grant Anticipatory Bail then the Applicant be directed to give undertaking in terms of order of the Supreme Court in the case of Abhijit Jitendra Lolage vs State of Maharashtra 1 and more particularly relies on following condition imposed by the Supreme Court in case of similar offences :- "It is deemed appropriate to impose the condition - "I, Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage do undertake to not deal with Gutkha, that is, Pan Masala with Tobacco". In case, the appellant - Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage violates the terms and conditions of bail, including the undertaking imposed, it would be open to the prosecution to seek cancellation of bail ". (Emphasis added) Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel appearing for the Applicant after taking the instructions submits that the Applicant will give the undertaking. (e) The Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such a person from disclosing the facts to the Court or to any Police personnel.
